description: Provenance of the vendored Fermix wire contracts. The canonical files live in the fermix repository under apps/fermix_core/priv/; this tree is a byte-identical copy pinned by CHECKSUMS.txt. scripts/verify_protocol_contract.sh asserts the two agree, and --source <fermix-checkout> byte-compares against upstream.

Protocol 3 on the 1 to 3 window: the floor stays 1, so a v1 pet still runs openai_realtime, and xai_realtime needs 3, refusing an older pet at call_start with update_required, required_for xai_realtime, before any provider session opens. A Grok call's audio_delta carries playback_id, a call-local id of at most 64 bytes, and the pet answers with playback_progress {playback_id, played_ms, drained}, at most every 100 ms while an id plays and at once when it drains or playback stops; the daemon refuses unknown_playback, playback_regressed and playback_beyond_sent, paces the reply to about ten seconds unplayed on the pet, and ends a call with playback_stalled (sent audio unreported for 2 seconds), playback_overflow or call_ids_exhausted. usage adds voice_text_items, and a Grok call's final accounting is always incomplete. The OpenAI engines' frames are unchanged, and playback_progress is refused under them. These bytes also take the engine's M56 frames this contract had held back since a53f739a: assistant_text_done, call_uuid, conversation and tasks_outlive_call on call_ready, call_uuid, server_seq and detached on task, call_uuid on usage, and the call_in_progress refusal. contracts.name: native_host
contracts.provenance_note: Re-pinned on 2026-10-21 at 95ee575b, the commit the engine's v0.16.0 tag names on main; every file is byte for byte the 411214c8 pin's. Vendored first on 2026-10-18 at 411214c8 on dev, the commit origin carries, so committed_upstream is true; its bytes are the ones M76's Snooze commit 4c813f55 published, and nothing under priv/native_host moved after it. The native host wire is the app's second host wire, beside the browser host and in its grammar, for a different concept: the app serves the daemon this Mac's own services, notifications first. It is newline-delimited JSON on native_host.sock in the Fermix home, mode 0600, served only by the Fermix app's own engine, with the browser host's trust check (a process the daemon started is refused untrusted_host), one host at a time (host_already_attached) and the browser host's 4,194,304-byte cap on the app's lines. Direction is reversed from the management, realtime and companion wires: the app completes client_hello/server_hello, sends attached {host_version} and then capabilities {notifications}, granted, not_granted or not_asked, read from the framework at attach and on every change, and the daemon is the one asking with a numbered id per request. Four requests: notifications.authorize, answering the grant state and raising the macOS prompt only while it is not_asked, never twice; notifications.post {title, body, sound, actions, reminder_id?}, answering notification_id, at most two actions of which snooze_10m is the one, and refused not_authorized unless granted or post_failed with the framework's own words; host.status, answering host_version and notifications; and host.stop_ack, the daemon's answer to the app's host_stopping that a held quit waits on. The app's events are attached, capabilities, notification.action {reminder_id, action}, the person's Snooze 10 minutes press, which the daemon applies with no model turn, and host_stopping. Four host error reasons answer a request without closing the connection (not_authorized, post_failed, invalid_request, host_unavailable), and fourteen daemon errors close it. Protocol 1 on the 1 to 1 window, since this is the wire's first version.
